sections.h2: What makes selling a house fast in Doral different?
sections.html:
Doral is a Miami-Dade city, so the county's separate deed tax rate, its property appraiser and its tax collector apply to your sale. Many Doral homes sit in community associations, so an HOA payoff or approval can matter as much as the price.

The city is small by area and dense with work. Its own About page puts Doral at 15 square miles with approximately 81,182 residents, and says more than 100,000 people work within the city. That workforce, close to Miami International Airport, keeps demand for housing steady.

  • List the house if you can wait for showings and lender timelines.
  • Sell as-is for cash if a move date, repairs or a tax deadline is pressing.
  • Ask your association about transfer fees, estoppel letters and approval steps early.

sections.h2: Where is Doral and how is it bounded?
sections.html:
Doral covers 15 square miles bounded on the west by the Ronald Reagan Turnpike, on the north by the Town of Medley, on the east by the Palmetto Expressway and on the south by the City of Sweetwater. It lies about one mile from Miami International Airport and twelve miles from Downtown Miami.

sections.h2: How did Doral grow from swampland to a city?
sections.html:
In the late 1950s a couple bought 2,400 acres of swampland to build a golf course and hotel, opened the Doral Hotel and Country Club in 1962, and combined their first names to make the name Doral. The city's history page tells the rest.

By the early 1980s, Doral Estates and then Doral Park were built and named after the hotel. From 1983 to 1985 the county imposed a building moratorium to protect well fields, and growth surged once it lifted. Early residents lived with few stores, schools or parks and relied on low housing costs.

In January 2003, after a seven year effort, 85 percent of voters backed incorporation, and in June 92 percent accepted the charter. The city now describes development in areas such as Downtown Doral, City Place Doral and Midtown Doral. Newer buildings in those areas often sit in condominium or townhome associations, which affects how a sale closes. Read the full Doral history.

sections.h2: What does Miami-Dade charge on a Doral deed?
sections.html:
Miami-Dade uses its own documentary stamp rate: 60 cents per $100 plus a 45 cents per $100 surtax, according to the Department of Revenue. The surtax is not due on a document transferring only a single-family dwelling.

That difference matters for a Doral seller. A single-family house avoids the surtax, while a condominium unit is not described by the Department of Revenue as a single-family dwelling, so ask the closing agent how the surtax applies to a condo or townhome. The state says all parties to the deed are liable regardless of who agrees to pay, and the clerk collects at recording.

Recording fees are separate: $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each additional page under section 28.24, plus trust fund and technology charges.

sections.h2: When are Miami-Dade property taxes due for a Doral home?
sections.html:
Florida's calendar applies: the tax collector sends bills in November, discounts step down from 4 percent in November to 1 percent in February, and unpaid taxes become delinquent on April 1. Tax certificates are sold on unpaid items by June 1.

  • The property appraiser mails the TRIM notice each August, and a value challenge petition goes to the clerk within 25 days of that notice.
  • Homestead exemption applications are due March 1 on Form DR-501.
  • The Miami-Dade Property Appraiser lists exemptions, assessment reductions and land use classifications on its exemptions page.

Update your mailing address so a November bill reaches you after a sale. Ask the Miami-Dade Tax Collector for the current payoff before closing.

sections.h2: How can I weigh a quick sale against listing in Doral?
sections.html:
Compare net proceeds, time and certainty. A listing adds showings and a buyer's lender. A cash buyer removes the loan, but you should ask about association approval, who pays stamps and the closing date.

  1. Get a mortgage payoff statement.
  2. Request an HOA estoppel letter if applicable.
  3. Confirm the tax bill status.
  4. Ask each buyer for written terms.

If a foreclosure is pending, the clerk's public sale comes 20 to 35 days after final judgment unless the plaintiff agrees to longer.

faqs.q: When did Doral become a city?
faqs.a: Doral was incorporated on January 28, 2003, as one of thirty-four municipalities in Miami-Dade County.
The city's About page lists 15 square miles and approximately 81,182 residents.

faqs.q: What is the Miami-Dade deed tax rate?
faqs.a: The Department of Revenue prints 60 cents per $100 plus a 45 cents per $100 surtax, with the surtax not due on a document transferring only a single-family dwelling.

faqs.q: When do Miami-Dade property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1, under the Florida tax calendar. Discounts run 4 percent in November down to 1 percent in February.

faqs.q: Does Doral have a building history that affects buyers?
faqs.a: Yes. The county imposed a building moratorium from 1983 to 1985 to protect well fields, and many neighborhoods began as Doral Estates and Doral Park.
